title: The continuum hypothesis is independent of ZFC
statement: If ZFC is consistent, then ZFC neither proves nor refutes the statement that every infinite set of real numbers is in bijection either with the natural numbers or with the reals.

formal.statement: ; NOT EXPRESSIBLE, on two independent counts. The statement quantifies over subsets of the reals, which is second order and outside any SMT-LIB logic; and the independence claim is about derivability in ZFC, which needs the same reflection machinery F:godel-first-incompleteness names. axeyum's Real sort is a first-order ordered field with no set-of-reals sort and no cardinality apparatus.

provenance.source: authored from the S:logic-and-proof strand of the math-education concept graph; statement written here, not copied

prior_art.citation: Godel 1940 (consistency of CH); Cohen 1963 (consistency of not-CH)

notes: Third and last of the deliberately-unstatable entries, chosen because it fails for a DIFFERENT reason than the other two and so maps a different edge of the frontier. F:godel-first-incompleteness and F:fol-validity-undecidable are blocked by the absence of reflection alone; this one is blocked by reflection AND by order -- there is no second-order quantification and no cardinality anywhere in the stack, and a 'complete framework for general reasoning' that intends to reach ordinary mathematics eventually has to answer for that. Recorded also as a warning label for the self-extension loop: an `open` fact with `formal.fragment: none` must never be dispatched to a solver, and a consumer that filters only on status will do exactly that.
